layer_definition: Model-independent verifier/scoring credibility: given the same final answer, patch, or task artifact, Loom must assign the same task-level reward and aggregate metric semantics as the canonical reference.

canonical_reference.title: AIME 2024 rows from AI-MO/aimo-validation-aime
canonical_reference.justification: AIME is scored as exact integer answer matching over the year-specific task set.

harbor_support.parity_target: exact-integer match against the canonical answer field on the AIME 2024 dataset row
harbor_support.decision: Harbor ships no AIME verifier. Loom's adapter (`AIME24Adapter.convert_instance`) emits a script verifier (`verifier/run.sh` + `verifier/check.py`) that extracts the last integer from `final_answer.txt` and compares to the canonical `answer` field. Equivalence is proven by replay against known correct and known incorrect answers.

score_semantics.task_set: AIME 2024 I/II tasks imported into the aime-24 benchmark.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable aime-24 task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the normalized final integer equals the canonical integer answer; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids

cases.reference: canonical answer integer from aime-24 task metadata
cases.replay_method: Replay a known correct final integer through the Loom verifier and the upstream/canonical integer scorer.

replay_tests.asserts: reward={'score': 1.0} when `final_answer.txt` ends with the canonical integer answer; structured output matches `{got, expected}`
reward={'score': 0.0} when the extracted integer differs from the canonical answer
the extraction rule is 'last integer on the final line', documented behavior matches the AIME single-integer answer convention

canonical_reference.title: AIME 2025 I rows from MathArena/aime_2025_I
canonical_reference.justification: AIME 2025 is scored as exact integer answer matching over the published MathArena task set used by Loom.

harbor_support.parity_target: exact-integer match against the canonical answer field on the AIME 2025 dataset row
harbor_support.decision: Same construction as aime-24 — the AIME 2025 adapter shares the same script-verifier infrastructure. The aime-25 adapter specifically emits the same `verifier/check.py` extractor; equivalence is proven by the aime-25 adapter test that asserts the script path is wired correctly.

score_semantics.task_set: AIME 2025 I tasks imported into the aime-25 benchmark.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable aime-25 task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the normalized final integer equals the canonical integer answer; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids

cases.reference: canonical answer integer from aime-25 task metadata
cases.replay_method: Replay a known correct boxed or final-line integer through the Loom verifier and the upstream/canonical integer scorer.

replay_tests.asserts: the aime-25 adapter wires the same script verifier path as aime-22..24 so the integer extraction + comparison logic is shared
the shared integer-extraction routine handles the canonical AIME answer shape — used by both aime-24 and aime-25 since they share verifier infrastructure

canonical_reference.title: GPQA Extended
canonical_reference.justification: GPQA Extended is a multiple-choice benchmark scored by exact choice accuracy.

harbor_support.decision: Use Harbor as parity target only after support is confirmed; otherwise replay identical selected choices against the upstream/canonical answer key.

score_semantics.task_set: GPQA extended test rows imported into the gpqa benchmark.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable gpqa task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the normalized selected choice matches the canonical answer; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids

cases.reference: canonical GPQA answer option from task metadata
cases.replay_method: Replay a known correct answer choice through Loom and the canonical answer-key scorer.

canonical_reference.title: MATH-500
canonical_reference.justification: MATH-500 is scored by normalized final answer equivalence over the selected 500-problem MATH subset.

harbor_support.decision: Use Harbor as parity target only after support is confirmed; otherwise replay identical final answers through the canonical MATH answer-normalization path.

score_semantics.task_set: HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500 test rows imported into math-500.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable math-500 task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the normalized final answer is equivalent to the canonical answer; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids

cases.reference: canonical MATH-500 answer from task metadata
cases.replay_method: Replay a known correct normalized final answer through Loom and the canonical MATH scorer.

canonical_reference.title: OpenAI HumanEval
canonical_reference.justification: HumanEval is scored by executing generated code against canonical tests and reporting pass@k; Loom v1 reports pass@1-style task reward for one submitted output.

harbor_support.parity_target: OpenAI HumanEval `check(candidate)` execution bundled with the task
harbor_support.decision: Harbor ships no HumanEval verifier. Loom's adapter (`HumanEvalAdapter.convert_instance`) emits the upstream check function verbatim into pytest-style test files, so Loom's pytest verifier IS the canonical scorer by construction.

score_semantics.task_set: openai/openai_humaneval test tasks imported into humaneval.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable humaneval task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when canonical tests pass for the submitted solution; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids for the selected pass@1 run

cases.reference: OpenAI HumanEval canonical test execution for one task
cases.replay_method: Replay a known passing solution through Loom pytest/script verifier and the canonical HumanEval execution harness.

replay_tests.asserts: reward=1.0 when the bundled `_reference.py` is copied into `solution.py` and pytest runs the upstream `check(candidate)`
reward!=1.0 when the agent's solution stub raises NotImplementedError

canonical_reference.title: LiveCodeBench code generation lite
canonical_reference.justification: LiveCodeBench code generation is scored by executing submitted code against hidden/public tests and reporting pass rate.

harbor_support.parity_target: LiveCodeBench upstream evaluator unless Harbor support is confirmed
harbor_support.decision: Replay identical code artifacts through Loom and the upstream LiveCodeBench evaluator before reporting deltas.

score_semantics.task_set: livecodebench/code_generation_lite test rows imported into livecodebench.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable livecodebench task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the submitted program passes the canonical tests for that task; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids
score_semantics.partial_credit: none for the current Loom per-task score

cases.reference: LiveCodeBench upstream evaluator for one code_generation_lite task
cases.replay_method: Replay a known passing solution through Loom and the pinned upstream LiveCodeBench evaluator.

canonical_reference.title: Google MBPP sanitized
canonical_reference.justification: MBPP is scored by executing generated Python against canonical tests and reporting pass@k; Loom v1 reports one-output pass@1-style reward.

harbor_support.parity_target: MBPP canonical tests bundled with the task
harbor_support.decision: Harbor (coder-harbor-cloud) ships only voyager bespoke tasks (fizzbuzz, hello-world, bugfix-sum). It does not ship an MBPP verifier. Loom's verifier IS the canonical MBPP pytest harness — the same upstream test strings are written verbatim into the materialized bundle by `MBPPAdapter.convert_instance`, so the verifier and the canonical scorer are the same code path by construction. Equivalence is proven by replay, not paired-runtime comparison.

score_semantics.task_set: sanitized MBPP test rows imported into mbpp.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable mbpp task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when canonical tests pass for the submitted solution; 0.0 otherwise
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids for the selected pass@1 run

cases.reference: MBPP canonical test execution for one sanitized task
cases.replay_method: Replay a known passing solution through Loom pytest/script verifier and the canonical MBPP tests.

replay_tests.asserts: reward=1.0 when the bundled `_reference.py` is copied into `solution.py` and pytest runs
reward!=1.0 (pytest returncode nonzero) when the stub `solution.py` is left in place — guards against the #388 false-positive class

cases.reference: canonical MMLU-Pro answer option from task metadata
cases.replay_method: Replay a known correct answer choice through Loom and the canonical MMLU-Pro answer-key scorer.

canonical_reference.title: SkillFlow task bundle
canonical_reference.justification: SkillFlow score credibility depends on replaying the same task artifact through the upstream task verifier semantics bundled with the dataset.

harbor_support.parity_target: upstream SkillFlow verifier unless Harbor support is confirmed
harbor_support.decision: Replay identical produced artifacts through Loom and the upstream SkillFlow verifier path.

score_semantics.task_set: SkillFlow tasks imported from the upstream task bundle.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable skillflow task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: numeric task verifier reward emitted by the upstream-compatible task harness
score_semantics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of task_reward over distinct task ids
score_semantics.partial_credit: allowed only when the upstream task verifier emits a fractional numeric reward

cases.reference: SkillFlow upstream-compatible verifier output for one task
cases.replay_method: Replay a known successful task artifact through Loom and the upstream-compatible SkillFlow verifier.

canonical_reference.title: SWE-Bench Verified
canonical_reference.justification: SWE-Bench Verified is scored by applying a patch and running repository-specific tests to determine resolved/unresolved.

harbor_support.parity_target: Harbor if supported, otherwise official SWE-Bench harness
harbor_support.decision: Replay identical patches through Loom and the confirmed Harbor/official SWE-Bench harness before treating resolved rate as credible.

score_semantics.task_set: SWE-Bench Verified test instances imported into swe-bench-verified.
score_semantics.denominator: number of runnable swe-bench-verified task ids
score_semantics.task_reward: 1.0 when the submitted patch resolves the instance according to canonical tests; 0.0 otherwise

cases.reference: official SWE-Bench harness result for one verified instance
cases.replay_method: Replay a known resolving patch through Loom and the official or Harbor SWE-Bench verifier.

canonical_reference.title: Terminal-Bench 2.0
canonical_reference.justification: Terminal-Bench 2.0 is scored by task-specific terminal verifier success under the pinned upstream task set.

harbor_support.parity_target: Terminal-Bench upstream evaluator unless Harbor support is confirmed
harbor_support.decision: Replay identical terminal task outputs/artifacts through Loom and the pinned upstream Terminal-Bench evaluator.
